intro: The convincing view can be the whole point. These images exaggerate observed detail, open a ceiling, move an image out of alignment or extend a film set.
alt: A highly detailed portrait, a ceiling figure seen from below, an angled wall projection and a painted city beyond the figure.

variants.name: hyperrealism
variants.look: Skin, glass and ceramics are treated with sharp detail at large scale.
variants.history: Hyperrealist painting and sculpture developed from approaches to photographs and observed detail in the later 20th century.
variants.when: Make an ordinary object worth prolonged close inspection.
variants.why: Enlargement and exact rendering make details that usually go unnoticed central to the image.

variants.name: illusionistic ceiling painting
variants.look: Foreshortened painted architecture opens the surface toward an apparent sky.
variants.history: Baroque ceiling painters such as Andrea Pozzo extended real architecture with painted perspective. A convincing view depends on where the viewer stands.
variants.when: Make an enclosed ceiling feel open or position viewers beneath a dramatic scene.
variants.why: Perspective lines seem to extend real space beyond the actual surface.

variants.name: anamorphosis
variants.look: The image is stretched over a corner and resolves when seen from a particular vantage point.
variants.history: Hans Holbein’s The Ambassadors contains a stretched skull that resolves when viewed obliquely. Related effects may use curved mirrors.
variants.when: Build an image that visitors discover by moving to a specific spot.
variants.why: Distorting construction makes the viewer’s position an active part of the design.

variants.name: matte painting
variants.look: Small-scale foreground details merge into a much larger painted city.
variants.history: Filmmakers used paintings to extend locations and sets, either by combining the painting and the filmed image or adding a background in the camera’s view.
variants.when: Show a distant environment beyond the resources of a built set.
variants.why: Match perspective and atmospheric light so the painted distance reads as part of the photographed space.

source.label: Academy Museum | Preserving a Vanishing Art
